mean: to give help just when it is badly needed
lit: to bring charcoal in the snow

use.how: Predicate or object of 是: 你这是雪中送炭。 Praises help given to someone in real trouble, often contrasted with 锦上添花.

near.diff: 锦上添花 adds to what is already good; 雪中送炭 rescues someone in hardship. The saying 锦上添花易，雪中送炭难 sets them against each other.
助人为乐 describes a person who enjoys helping in general; 雪中送炭 is one act of help at a moment of crisis.

cue: Your shop was about to close for lack of cash, and an old friend lent you money without being asked. How do you describe his help?

ctx.s: 我失业的时候，你借钱给我，真是{雪中送炭}。
ctx.en: You lent me money when I lost my job; that was real help when I needed it most.

ctx.s: 地震后第一批救援物资到达，对灾区来说是{雪中送炭}。
ctx.en: The first relief supplies to arrive after the earthquake were a lifeline for the stricken area.

ctx.s: 这笔贷款对快要倒闭的小工厂无异于{雪中送炭}。
ctx.en: For a small factory on the verge of closing, this loan is nothing less than a rescue.

ctx.s: “雨这么大，车又坏了，幸好你来接我。”“小事，算不上{雪中送炭}。”
ctx.en: "In this downpour, with my car broken down, thank goodness you came to get me." "It's nothing, hardly a rescue."

ctx.s: 锦上添花的人很多，愿意{雪中送炭}的人却很少。
ctx.en: Plenty of people will add to your success, but few will help you when you are struggling.

ctx.s: 那年冬天他家里出了事，村里人送来粮食和衣服，这份{雪中送炭}的情谊他一直记着。
ctx.en: That winter his family hit trouble, and the villagers brought food and clothes; he never forgot the kindness they showed him in his hour of need.

bad.s: 他已经是冠军了，我们再送他一辆车，真是{雪中送炭}。
bad.en: (meant: he is already champion and we gave him a car on top)
bad.why: Giving more to someone who is already doing well is jǐn shàng tiān huā; this idiom needs a person in trouble.

bad.s: 今天下雪了，我{雪中送炭}去学校。
bad.en: (meant: it snowed today and I went to school)
bad.why: It is a figurative phrase for timely help, not a description of snowy weather or of carrying anything.

use.how: Usually a whole clause at the start of a sentence, often followed by 日月如梭: 光阴似箭，转眼十年过去了。 Said when looking back on how much time has passed.

near.diff: 不知不觉 means without noticing and can describe any change; 光阴似箭 is a sigh about how fast the years go by.

cue: At a class reunion you realise it has been twenty years since you graduated. What do you sigh about the years?

ctx.s: 真是{光阴似箭}，孩子一下子就上大学了。
ctx.en: Time really flies; suddenly the kids are off to university.

ctx.s: {光阴似箭}，日月如梭，转眼我们毕业已经十年了。
ctx.en: The years have flown by; in the blink of an eye it's been ten years since we graduated.

ctx.s: 爷爷看着老照片说：“{光阴似箭}啊，那时候我才二十岁。”
ctx.en: Looking at the old photos, Grandpa said, "How time flies. I was only twenty then."

ctx.s: 新年致辞里，校长说{光阴似箭}，希望大家珍惜在校的时光。
ctx.en: In his New Year speech the principal said that time flies and urged everyone to treasure their school years.

ctx.s: 回到故乡，他不禁感叹{光阴似箭}，当年的小镇已经变成了一座城市。
ctx.en: Back in his hometown, he couldn't help sighing at how time had flown: the little town of those days had become a city.

ctx.s: 难道你不觉得{光阴似箭}吗？好像昨天我们才刚认识。
ctx.en: Don't you feel time just flies? It seems we only met yesterday.

bad.s: 他跑得{光阴似箭}，第一个到了终点。
bad.en: (meant: he ran as fast as an arrow and finished first)
bad.why: It is only about time passing quickly, never about the speed of a person or a thing.

bad.s: 这个会议{光阴似箭}，开了五个小时。
bad.en: (meant: the meeting dragged on for five hours)
bad.why: It says time went by fast, the opposite of a long, tedious meeting, and it is about years, not hours.

lit: to fight for minutes and seize seconds

use.how: Predicate or adverbial with 地: 大家争分夺秒地工作。 Said of people working flat out to finish something urgent before a deadline.

near.diff: 迫在眉睫 describes a situation as urgent; 争分夺秒 describes people hurrying to deal with it.

cue: Rescuers dig through the rubble day and night, knowing every minute counts for the people trapped underneath. How do they work?

ctx.s: 考试前一周，他每天都在{争分夺秒}地复习。
ctx.en: In the week before the exam he revised every day as if every minute counted.

ctx.s: 救援人员{争分夺秒}，终于把被困的人救了出来。
ctx.en: Racing against time, the rescuers finally got the trapped people out.

ctx.s: 医生们在手术室里{争分夺秒}，抢救受伤的司机。
ctx.en: In the operating theatre the doctors fought against the clock to save the injured driver.

ctx.s: “还有十分钟就截止了！”“别说话了，{争分夺秒}吧！”
ctx.en: "Ten minutes until the deadline!" "Stop talking and let's not waste a second!"

ctx.s: 为了赶在雨季前完工，工人们日夜{争分夺秒}地施工。
ctx.en: To finish before the rainy season, the workers built day and night against the clock.

ctx.s: 在这场比赛里，选手们必须{争分夺秒}，一点儿也不能犹豫。
ctx.en: In this race the competitors must make every second count and can't hesitate at all.

bad.s: 我们俩为了一个座位{争分夺秒}，吵了起来。
bad.en: (meant: the two of us fought over a seat)
bad.why: Despite the words for fight and seize, it is about using time to the full, not about competing for an object.

bad.s: 我们要{争分夺秒}时间，早点完成任务。
bad.en: (meant: we must make good use of time and finish early)
bad.why: It is complete in itself and takes no object; adding a word for time after it is redundant and ungrammatical.

mean: there is plenty of time ahead
lit: the days ahead are still long

use.how: Usually a short clause of comfort or postponement: 别急，来日方长。 Said to reassure someone that there will be more chances later.

cue: A friend apologises at the airport for not having had time to show you around. You reassure her you will meet again. What do you say?

ctx.s: 这次没见到面没关系，{来日方长}嘛。
ctx.en: Never mind that we didn't get to meet this time; there will be other chances.

ctx.s: 你还年轻，{来日方长}，一次失败不算什么。
ctx.en: You're still young and have plenty of time ahead; one failure is nothing.

ctx.s: “今天没时间好好聊了。”“{来日方长}，下次再说。”
ctx.en: "We didn't get time to talk properly today." "There's plenty of time; let's catch up next time."

ctx.s: 临别时，老师拍拍他的肩膀，说了一句{来日方长}。
ctx.en: As they parted, the teacher patted his shoulder and said there would be time enough later.

ctx.s: 既然{来日方长}，我们何必急着今天就做决定呢？
ctx.en: Since we have plenty of time ahead, why rush to decide today?

ctx.s: 合作的事不着急，{来日方长}，咱们慢慢谈。
ctx.en: There's no hurry about working together; we have time, let's talk it over gradually.

bad.s: 这座古庙{来日方长}，已经有五百年了。
bad.en: (meant: this old temple has a long history of five hundred years)
bad.why: It looks forward to future time; a long past is described with lì shǐ yōu jiǔ.

bad.s: 明天早上八点就要交报告，{来日方长}，慢慢写吧。
bad.en: (meant: the report is due at eight tomorrow, take it easy)
bad.why: It means many chances in the future; it makes no sense about a deadline only hours away.

use.how: Predicate after 对……, often with 至今 or 仍然: 我对那天的事至今记忆犹新。 Said of a past event, usually a striking one, that one still remembers vividly.

cue: Years later, you can still picture exactly how your hands shook on the day of your first job interview. How do you describe that memory?

ctx.s: 第一次上台演讲的情景，我到现在还{记忆犹新}。
ctx.en: I still remember vividly what it was like the first time I gave a speech on stage.

ctx.s: 很多老人对那场大洪水至今{记忆犹新}。
ctx.en: Many old people still remember that great flood as if it were yesterday.

ctx.s: 虽然过去了二十年，她对那次旅行依然{记忆犹新}。
ctx.en: Although twenty years have passed, that trip is still fresh in her memory.

ctx.s: “你还记得我们第一次见面吗？”“当然，{记忆犹新}啊。”
ctx.en: "Do you remember the first time we met?" "Of course, I remember it like it was yesterday."

ctx.s: 去年那场比赛的结局让球迷们{记忆犹新}。
ctx.en: The ending of last year's match is still fresh in the fans' minds.

ctx.s: 他在回忆录中写道，入学那天的一切仍然{记忆犹新}。
ctx.en: In his memoir he wrote that everything about his first day at school was still vivid in his mind.

bad.s: 他的{记忆犹新}，什么都记得住。
bad.en: (meant: he has a good memory and remembers everything)
bad.why: It describes a particular past event staying vivid, not a person's ability to memorise.

bad.s: 我对下个月的旅行计划{记忆犹新}。
bad.en: (meant: I'm clear about next month's travel plans)
bad.why: It can only be said of something already in the past, not of a future plan.

lit: entirely like what has already gone by

use.how: Mostly an adverbial with 地 before a verb: 我们会一如既往地支持你。 Says an attitude or practice continues unchanged; common in formal statements and thanks.

near.diff: 一成不变 criticises rigidity and refusal to change; 一如既往 approvingly says a good attitude or effort continues.

cue: A company thanks its customers in a year-end letter and promises its service will stay as good as it has always been. Which phrase does it use?

ctx.s: 谢谢大家，希望你们{一如既往}地支持我们。
ctx.en: Thank you all; we hope you will keep supporting us as you always have.

ctx.s: 退休以后，他还是{一如既往}地每天早上跑步。
ctx.en: After retiring he still went running every morning, just as he always had.

ctx.s: 无论遇到什么困难，父母都{一如既往}地相信她。
ctx.en: Whatever difficulties she ran into, her parents believed in her just as they always had.

ctx.s: 这家餐馆换了老板，菜的味道却{一如既往}。
ctx.en: The restaurant changed owners, but the food tastes just as it always did.

ctx.s: “你们会继续合作吗？”“当然，我们会{一如既往}地合作下去。”
ctx.en: "Will you continue working together?" "Of course, we'll keep working together just as before."

ctx.s: 公司在声明中表示，将{一如既往}地重视产品质量。
ctx.en: In its statement the company said it would continue to put product quality first, as it always has.

bad.s: 我昨天{一如既往}地第一次去了北京。
bad.en: (meant: yesterday I went to Beijing for the first time)
bad.why: It means continuing as before, so it cannot describe something done for the first time.

bad.s: 他的想法太{一如既往}了，从来不肯改变。
bad.en: (meant: his thinking is too rigid and never changes)
bad.why: It is not a criticism of rigidity and cannot be graded with 'too'; for that meaning use yī chéng bù biàn.

mean: looking brand new after a change

use.how: Predicate, often after 变得 or with 让/使: 装修后，房子焕然一新。 Said of places, objects or appearances that look fresh after renovation or cleaning.

near.diff: 面目全非 is unrecognisable, usually for the worse; 焕然一新 is a welcome fresh new look.
日新月异 is rapid ongoing change over time; 焕然一新 is the bright new result of one makeover.

cue: After a weekend of painting the walls and changing the curtains, your tired old flat looks bright and fresh. How does it look now?

ctx.s: 重新粉刷以后，教室{焕然一新}。
ctx.en: After being repainted, the classroom looked brand new.

ctx.s: 妈妈把厨房打扫了一遍，整个厨房变得{焕然一新}。
ctx.en: Mom gave the kitchen a thorough clean, and the whole kitchen looked like new.

ctx.s: 老街经过改造，{焕然一新}，吸引了很多游客。
ctx.en: After the renovation the old street looks fresh and new and draws lots of tourists.

ctx.s: “你换发型了？”“对啊，是不是整个人{焕然一新}？”
ctx.en: "Did you change your hairstyle?" "Yes, don't I look like a new person?"

ctx.s: 春节前，家家户户贴上春联，让村子显得{焕然一新}。
ctx.en: Before Spring Festival every household puts up couplets, giving the village a fresh new look.

ctx.s: 这家老酒店重新开业，大堂的设计{焕然一新}。
ctx.en: The old hotel has reopened, and the lobby has a completely fresh design.

bad.s: 大火之后，这栋楼{焕然一新}，只剩下黑色的墙。
bad.en: (meant: after the fire the building was utterly changed, only black walls left)
bad.why: It is always a positive fresh look; damage beyond recognition is miàn mù quán fēi.

bad.s: 他学了一年中文，水平{焕然一新}。
bad.en: (meant: after a year of study his Chinese improved a lot)
bad.why: It describes a visible new appearance of places or things, not progress in skills.

lit: the face and features are entirely not what they were

use.how: Predicate, often after 变得 or 被……改得: 原文被改得面目全非。 Usually regrets that something was damaged or distorted until unrecognisable.

near.diff: 焕然一新 is a welcome fresh look; 面目全非 is so changed it is no longer itself, usually for the worse.
翻天覆地 is sweeping, often positive change in society or life; 面目全非 regrets that something lost its original form.

cue: You wrote a short story, and the editor rewrote it so heavily that you can no longer find your own ideas in it. What happened to your story?

ctx.s: 我的作文被他改得{面目全非}。
ctx.en: He rewrote my essay until it was unrecognisable.

ctx.s: 一场台风过后，海边的小村庄{面目全非}。
ctx.en: After the typhoon, the little seaside village was damaged beyond recognition.

ctx.s: 这部电影把原著改得{面目全非}，很多读者都很失望。
ctx.en: The film changed the original novel beyond recognition, and many readers were disappointed.

ctx.s: “你还认得你小时候住的那条街吗？”“不认得了，早就{面目全非}了。”
ctx.en: "Do you still recognise the street you grew up on?" "No, it changed beyond recognition long ago."

ctx.s: 那辆车撞得{面目全非}，司机却奇迹般地没受重伤。
ctx.en: The car was wrecked beyond recognition, yet the driver miraculously escaped serious injury.

ctx.s: 经过几次随意的修补，这座古桥已经{面目全非}了。
ctx.en: After several careless repairs, the old bridge has lost all trace of its original look.

bad.s: 新公园修得{面目全非}，漂亮极了！
bad.en: (meant: the new park was beautifully transformed)
bad.why: It regrets loss of the original form; praise for a beautiful makeover needs huàn rán yī xīn.

bad.s: 他对我{面目全非}，一点儿也不客气。
bad.en: (meant: he was rude to me)
bad.why: It describes the state of a thing that has been changed, not how a person treats someone.

mean: to let things take their natural course

use.how: Predicate, often in advice: 别想太多，顺其自然吧。 Said about things one cannot or should not force, such as feelings, health or outcomes.

near.diff: 随机应变 is actively adjusting to a changing situation; 顺其自然 is not forcing anything and letting events unfold.

cue: Your friend keeps worrying whether a first date will turn into a relationship. You tell her not to force it and see what happens. What do you advise?

ctx.s: 感情的事不能勉强，{顺其自然}吧。
ctx.en: You can't force matters of the heart; just let things take their course.

ctx.s: 孩子什么时候开口说话，家长不用太着急，{顺其自然}就好。
ctx.en: Parents needn't worry about when their child starts talking; it will come naturally.

ctx.s: “考不上怎么办？”“尽力就行，结果{顺其自然}。”
ctx.en: "What if I don't pass?" "Just do your best and let the result be what it will be."

ctx.s: 医生说失眠时不要强迫自己睡，要学会{顺其自然}。
ctx.en: The doctor said not to force yourself to sleep when you have insomnia, but to learn to let it come.

ctx.s: 他对升职的事看得很开，一切都{顺其自然}。
ctx.en: He's relaxed about promotion and lets everything take its natural course.

ctx.s: 既然我们已经努力过了，何不{顺其自然}呢？
ctx.en: Since we've already done our best, why not just let things take their course?

bad.s: 他做事很{顺其自然}，所以总是迟到。
bad.en: (meant: he is easygoing, so he is always late)
bad.why: It is a stance towards outcomes one cannot control, not a word for a lazy or casual personality.

bad.s: 老板突然改了计划，他马上{顺其自然}，想出了新办法。
bad.en: (meant: when the boss changed the plan he quickly adapted and found a new way)
bad.why: Quick active adjustment to a new situation is suí jī yìng biàn; this idiom means letting things happen.

mean: when in Rome, do as the Romans do
lit: on entering a village, follow its customs

use.how: Usually a short clause of advice or explanation: 既然来了，就入乡随俗吧。 Said about adapting to the customs of a new place or group.

near.diff: 随机应变 is reacting flexibly to any change of situation; 入乡随俗 is specifically following local customs in a new place.

cue: On your first trip to Japan you take off your shoes at the door and bow when greeting people, just as the locals do. What principle are you following?

ctx.s: 到了日本，我们也{入乡随俗}，进门先脱鞋。
ctx.en: In Japan we did as the locals do and took our shoes off at the door.

ctx.s: 他第一次在四川吃火锅，虽然怕辣，还是{入乡随俗}点了辣锅。
ctx.en: His first time eating hotpot in Sichuan, he was afraid of spice but did as the locals do and ordered the spicy broth.

ctx.s: “这儿的人吃饭都用手吗？”“对，{入乡随俗}嘛，你也试试。”
ctx.en: "Do people here eat with their hands?" "Yes. When in Rome, you know; give it a try."

ctx.s: 出国留学要学会{入乡随俗}，尊重当地的习惯。
ctx.en: When you study abroad, you need to learn to adapt and respect local customs.

ctx.s: 新同事刚从国外来，现在也{入乡随俗}，每天中午跟我们一起午睡。
ctx.en: Our new colleague only just arrived from abroad, but she has adopted the local habit and naps after lunch with us every day.

ctx.s: 既然住在这个小镇，何不{入乡随俗}，参加大家的节日活动？
ctx.en: Since you live in this little town, why not join in and take part in everyone's festivals?

bad.s: 他{入乡随俗}，回到了自己的老家。
bad.en: (meant: he went back to his hometown)
bad.why: It is about adapting to someone else's customs, not about the act of going to or returning to a place.

bad.s: 天气变冷了，我们{入乡随俗}，多穿点衣服。
bad.en: (meant: it got cold so we wore more clothes)
bad.why: It concerns local customs of a place or group, not adjusting to weather or general circumstances.
